tested_scope.question: Can a public read-only GitHub endpoint distinguish history A (candidate tag name never used) from history B (same tag name previously backed an immutable release, then the immutable release and tag were deleted), without creating/updating a ref or release?
tested_scope.history_A: Current repository has no current tag ref t and no current published release for t; t has never backed an immutable release.
tested_scope.history_B: t previously backed an immutable release; that immutable release was deleted; its tag was then deleted; current repository has no current tag ref t and no current published release for t. The repository-resurrection variant is included only to the extent explicitly documented by GitHub's immutable-release anti-reuse statement.
documented_read_surfaces_checked: GET published release by tag t
immutable-releases documentation for any documented per-tag read-visible reservation/floor surface
excluded: protected/admin configuration as an outcome dependency

public_sources.observation: GitHub documents that after deleting an immutable release, its tag can be deleted but the same tag name cannot be reused; the protection also survives repository delete/recreate with the same name. This proves a service-side historical anti-reuse rule exists, not that it is exposed by a read endpoint.
Get a reference returns 404 when the requested ref does not currently exist. Therefore after tag deletion, this endpoint has the same documented result for A and B.
Get a release by tag name returns 404 Resource not found when no current published release is found. Therefore after release deletion, this endpoint has the same documented result for A and B.

dimensions: same current repository versus documented repository-resurrection variant
finite_model.write_time_hidden_difference: B is documented as unable to reuse the historical immutable-release tag name, while A is not known to carry that historical reservation. Observing this difference requires a write-time attempt or another currently undocumented read surface.

result.new_falsification: Within the bounded documented surfaces checked, immutable-release tag-name anti-reuse is not a stateless read-visible freshness floor. The two histories are read-indistinguishable after deletion on current ref and current release-by-tag GETs.
result.new_positive_evidence: The hidden service-side anti-reuse state is still useful as a write-time duplicate-name fence because GitHub explicitly documents that a used immutable-release tag name cannot be reused even after release/tag deletion and repository resurrection.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: A repository/target-native non-mutating read surface or sink-side enforcement rule that exposes or enforces a monotonic minimum generation across deletion/recreation and cannot be bypassed by a distinct previously-unused stale transition identifier.

observed_documented: immutable-release historical tag name cannot be reused after deletion and repository resurrection
observation_inference_split.inference: No read-visible per-tag reservation endpoint was found in this bounded documentation pass; this is not evidence that undocumented/internal state is absent.

phase1_acceptance.scope_guard: Applies only to the documented GitHub read surfaces listed above and the explicit immutable-release anti-reuse semantics. It does not generalize to arbitrary external sinks or undocumented APIs.
